newsitem.title: UK: C&W gains ahead of CWC flotation.
newsitem.headline: C&W gains ahead of CWC flotation.

text.p: Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc (C&W) pushed ahead gently on Monday ahead of the flotation of Cable & Wireless Communications (CWC), dealers said.
C&W shares were up 3.5 pence, or 0.74 percent, to 475p by 0830 GMT in volume of 310,000 while the FTSE-100 index was 5.2 points, or 0.12 percent, lower at 4364.5.
CWC, Britain's biggest and newest cable telephone and television group, said last Friday it was likely to float a 14.7 percent stake in London and New York on Monday.
While CWC has an estimated value of around 4.5 billion stg ($7.2 billion), its 14.7 percent flotation would not be big enough to propel CWC into the FTSE-100, analysts said.
Analysts expected trading to begin at 1330 GMT to coincide with the opening of the New York stock exchange.
CWC, majority-owned by C&W, was formed in 1996 by merging the Mercury unit of C&W with the three British cable TV units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada.
